text:
alex_m: quick heads-up — after yesterday's kernel selector change the /rerank-embed p99 climbed ~30% in canary, can anyone help bisect?

priya_s: do you have the numbers and the workload config? synthetic or replay?

alex_m: perf-bot posted the CI run but TL;DR: p50 ~45ms -> 48ms, p99 220ms -> 310ms, throughput (rps) ~unchanged. Using replay harness against recorded traffic from prod-like trace. Run id: replay/2026-03-16/6732.

alex_m: command I used to reproduce locally:
```
./harness/replay --trace traces/20260316-rerank.json --endpoint /v1/rerank-embed --concurrency 32 --qps 250 \\\n  --batch-max-tokens 4096 --batch-min-items 4 --keep-alive=true \
  --kv-warmup=true --vector-dim 1536
```
results attached to perf-bot report.

perf-bot: CI perf summary (master -> kernel-select-2026-03-15):
- workload: replay (mixed queries)
- p50: 48ms -> 50ms (+4%)
- p95: 140ms -> 200ms (+43%)
- p99: 220ms -> 310ms (+41%)
- 99.9: 480ms -> 860ms (+79%)
run: ci/perf/176842/rt-8

sam_g: interesting — my hunch is kernel selection fallback path is picking a generic GEMM for small sequence lengths instead of the optimized attention+fused matmul. That increases latency variance (tail). Can we force the older selection logic and compare?

jing_w: also worth checking batching heuristics: replay traffic tends to produce many small batches (1-3 items) and a few large batches; synthetic uniform load hides that. Please run both: (1) synthetic fixed-batch size 8, (2) replay. We need apples-to-apples on same model build and kernel toggles.

alex_m: will run a 4-way matrix: vector dims {384,1536} x payload {2KB,20KB} x kernel toggle {new,old} x traffic {synthetic,replay}. starting now, posting commands.

priya_s: don't forget cold vs warm KV cache. If replay includes many queries sharing prefixes, warm cache reduces cost. We should capture cold-start runs (new worker) vs steady-state. Also capture per-request KV cache hits metric.

sam_g: add this small toggle in the runtime for bisect: 
```
RUNTIME_KERN_SEL=force_old_kernel ./bin/serve --model rerank-v1 --port 8080
```
and compare p99. Also pin threads to NUMA nodes (pinning reduces jitter).

perf-bot: quick follow-up after kernel toggle test (run id: local/176843): forcing old kernel -> p99 235ms (back near baseline). Forcing new kernel -> p99 312ms. Suggests selection logic or new kernel microbehavior causing tail.

infra-ci: added a perf job to nightly that runs the replay harness with 1536-dim vectors and payloads sampled from prod. Job name: nightly/replay-rerank-tail.

alex_m: OK opening perf ticket PRF-412 with bisect notes, attaching trace + perf-bot outputs + run matrix. Assigning to @sam_g and @jing_w to finish kernel bisect and KV cache warmup experiments.

priya_s: thanks — next steps: 1) reproduce this locally with the exact replay trace, 2) run cold-start experiments (spawn new worker and run 100 queries), 3) run synthetic fixed-batch tests for baseline. Post raw histograms (counts per ms) so we can compare tails. :thumbsup:

sam_g: will take ownership of the kernel bisect tomorrow AM. I'll also add a microprofile hook around the attention kernels to see hotspot times (ms per call).

jing_w: I'll run the vector-dim / payload matrix and capture KV hit ratios. If we see pattern (e.g., large payloads push different memcpy path) that'll be useful.

alex_m: perfect — thanks everyone. keep notes in PRF-412 thread.

perf-bot: note: attaching flamegraphs for forced-old vs forced-new kernels to the ticket (s3://perf-artifacts/prf-412/).

alex_m: filing the doc and leaving instructions for reproducing in the ticket — will follow up after bisect results.
